181	# Scaffold or update project-local .claude/settings.json so Claude Code's
182	# /plan files land in ./.claude/plans/ (kept inside the repo) instead of the
183	# user-global plansDirectory. Pairs well with the agent-history-hygiene skill,
184	# which can then redact + commit the plan files alongside the diff.
185	#
186	# Also offers to import "orphan" plans — plans previously written under the
187	# global ~/.claude/plans/ that belong to this project. Detection: scan
188	# ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl (where Claude Code logs sessions
189	# per cwd; encoding maps '/' and '.' to '-') for Write/Edit tool_use entries
190	# whose file_path points into ~/.claude/plans/. This avoids false positives
191	# from sessions that merely *mentioned* a plan path in conversation.
192	#
193	# Usage: claude-plans-here [-f] [-y]
194	#   -f   auto-yes the settings.json merge prompt
195	#   -y   auto-yes the orphan-plan copy prompt
196	claude-plans-here() {
197	  emulate -L zsh
198	  local force_settings=0 force_orphans=0
199	  while (( $# > 0 )); do
200	    case "$1" in
201	      -f) force_settings=1 ;;
202	      -y) force_orphans=1 ;;
203	      -h|--help)
204	        echo "Usage: claude-plans-here [-f] [-y]"
205	        echo "  -f   auto-yes the settings.json merge prompt"
206	        echo "  -y   auto-yes the orphan-plan copy prompt"
207	        return 0
208	        ;;
209	      *)
210	        echo "claude-plans-here: unknown flag '$1'" >&2
211	        return 1
212	        ;;
213	    esac
214	    shift
215	  done
216	
217	  local target=".claude/settings.json"
218	  mkdir -p .claude/plans
219	
220	  if [[ ! -e "$target" ]]; then
221	    cat >"$target" <<'EOF'
222	{
223	  "plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"
224	}
225	EOF
226	    echo "Wrote $PWD/$target"
227	  else
228	    if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
229	      echo "claude-plans-here: jq required to merge into existing $target" >&2
230	      return 1
231	    fi
232	
233	    local ans=y
234	    if (( ! force_settings )); then
235	      read -q "ans?$target exists. Merge plansDirectory into it? [y/N] " || { echo; ans=n; }
236	      echo
237	    fi
238	
239	    if [[ "$ans" == [yY] ]]; then
240	      local tmp
241	      tmp="$(mktemp)" || return 1
242	      if jq --arg p "./.claude/plans" '. + {plansDirectory: $p}' "$target" >"$tmp"; then
243	        mv "$tmp" "$target"
244	        echo "Merged plansDirectory into $PWD/$target"
245	      else
246	        rm -f "$tmp"
247	        echo "claude-plans-here: jq failed; $target unchanged" >&2
248	        return 1
249	      fi
250	    fi
251	  fi
252	
253	  _claude_plans_here_import_orphans "$force_orphans"
254	}
255	
256	# Internal: scan ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd|encoded-git-root>/*.jsonl
257	# for Write/Edit tool_use entries that wrote into ~/.claude/plans/, list the
258	# ones still living in the global dir and not yet copied locally, prompt y/N.
259	_claude_plans_here_import_orphans() {
260	  emulate -L zsh
261	  setopt local_options null_glob
262	  local force="$1"
263	  local global_plans="$HOME/.claude/plans"
264	  [[ -d "$global_plans" ]] || return 0
265	
266	  # Claude Code projects/ encoding: replace each '/' and '.' with '-'.
267	  local enc_cwd="${PWD//\//-}"
268	  enc_cwd="${enc_cwd//./-}"
269	  local groot="" enc_root=""
270	  if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 && groot="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"; then
271	    if [[ -n "$groot" && "$groot" != "$PWD" ]]; then
272	      enc_root="${groot//\//-}"
273	      enc_root="${enc_root//./-}"
274	    fi
275	  fi
276	
277	  local -a proj_dirs
278	  [[ -d "$HOME/.claude/projects/$enc_cwd" ]] && proj_dirs+=("$HOME/.claude/projects/$enc_cwd")
279	  [[ -n "$enc_root" && -d "$HOME/.claude/projects/$enc_root" ]] && proj_dirs+=("$HOME/.claude/projects/$enc_root")
280	  (( ${#proj_dirs} == 0 )) && return 0
281	
282	  local -a jsonl_files
283	  local d
284	  for d in "${proj_dirs[@]}"; do
285	    jsonl_files+=("$d"/*.jsonl)
286	  done
287	  (( ${#jsonl_files} == 0 )) && return 0
288	
289	  # Two-stage filter: only lines containing a Write/Edit tool_use, then
290	  # extract any plan-path within them. Authoritative — avoids matching plan
291	  # paths that merely appeared in user/assistant text.
292	  local re_prefix="${global_plans//./\\.}"

# =============================================================================

# Load all .zsh files from a directory (sorted by filename)
load_zsh_dir() {
    local dir="$1"
    [[ -d "$dir" ]] || return 0
    setopt local_options null_glob
    local f
    for f in "$dir"/*.zsh; do
        [[ -r "$f" ]] && source "$f"

1	# aisuggest — prompt-time NL→shell ghost text via the existing _aiagent_invoke
2	# layer. Press the trigger (Alt+; default) to translate the current BUFFER from
3	# natural language into a single shell command, shown as ghost text. Tab or →
4	# accepts; any other keypress dismisses.
5	#
6	# Integrates with 04_ai_capture.zsh (_aiagent_invoke / _aiagent_autodetect) so
7	# the same agent autodetect (claude → opencode → codex → cursor-agent) and the
8	# same AICAP_*_MODEL defaults apply. No API key needed when claude / opencode /
9	# codex / cursor-agent CLIs are authenticated.
10	#
11	# Env-var defaults (set in ~/.zshrc.adhoc or ~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh to
12	# override; do not edit this file):
13	#
14	#   AISUGGEST_KEY              default: ^[;            (Alt+;)
15	#   AISUGGEST_AGENT            default: empty          (autodetect at invoke)
16	#   AISUGGEST_MODEL            default: empty          (use AICAP_*_MODEL)
17	#   AISUGGEST_HIGHLIGHT        default: fg=8           (region_highlight style)
18	#   AISUGGEST_PROMPT_OVERRIDE  default: empty          (replace built-in prompt)
19	#   AISUGGEST_DEBUG            default: 0              (1 = log every widget step
20	#                                                       to $AISUGGEST_LOG;
21	#                                                       runtime-toggleable)
22	#   AISUGGEST_LOG              default: /tmp/aisuggest.log
23	#
24	# Debugging:
25	#   `aisuggest "<text>"`              CLI form — same pipeline as the widget,
26	#                                     prints the suggestion to stdout.
27	#   `aisuggest --debug "<text>"`      Also prints raw / sanitized / final to
28	#                                     stderr layer-by-layer.
29	#   `export AISUGGEST_DEBUG=1`        Trace every widget step to $AISUGGEST_LOG.
30	#
31	# Architecture + design notes: docs/tools/zsh-inline-ai.md
32	#
33	# Roadmap (full rationale + upstream pointers in the doc above, "Roadmap" section):
34	#   1. Low-latency claude flag profile — bypass _aiagent_invoke for `agent==claude`,
35	#      shell out with `--no-session-persistence --effort low --no-chrome --tools ""
36	#      --setting-sources "" --system-prompt "$sys" "$user_input"`. ~1.5x faster.
37	#      Upstream ref: providers/claude-code.zsh.
38	#   2. Pass system prompt via `--system-prompt` flag instead of concatenating into
39	#      the user message. Tighter rule-following.
40	#   3. Async via `zle -F <fd>`. Currently we block the prompt during the agent call.
41	#      A non-blocking flow (background agent → FD watcher → render-on-arrival) lets
42	#      the user keep typing while the suggestion renders.
43	#   4. Direct API providers (anthropic / openai / gemini via curl + jq) for users

45	#      env var (1Password / pass / GNOME Keyring / AWS Secrets Manager).
46	#   5. Sanitize regression test (port upstream's test-sanitize.sh — crafted ANSI /
47	#      control-char payloads → assert _aisuggest_sanitize strips them).
48	#   6. Per-agent model env vars (AISUGGEST_CLAUDE_MODEL, AISUGGEST_OPENCODE_MODEL, …)
49	#      so users can pin different models per agent without re-exporting on switch.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-06 14:14:28Z)**_

評估完 `dot_config/zsh/`（41 個檔案、約 5000 行），結論：**技術上可行但效益偏低，且會明顯犧牲互動體驗**。

## 可復用的部分（約 60-70%）

純 env / alias / 工具 init 大多是 POSIX-friendly，幾乎都能直接共用：

- `00_exports.zsh.tmpl`、`02_legacy_tools.zsh` — PATH、Homebrew shellenv、GFW mirrors、GOPATH、BUN_INSTALL、PNPM_HOME — bash 也吃。
- 工具初始化幾乎全部都有 `init bash`：starship、fzf、zoxide、mise、direnv、thefuck、conda、cargo env、bat/eza、tldr、yazi、lazygit、tmux 整合、ssh-agent、bitwarden — 直接換 `init bash`/`bash` flag 即可。
- `10_aliases.zsh` 裡多數 alias 是 POSIX；少數函式 (`gundo`、`gcam-amend`、`brew-mirror`) 改寫成本低。

做法：把這層抽出成 `dot_config/shell/` 共用層，zsh 和 bash 都 source。

## 必須重寫或捨棄的部分（約 30%，但是「最有感」的功能）

這些都是 zsh-only 的互動 UX，bash 沒有對應：

| 功能 | zsh 機制 | bash 處境 |
|---|---|---|
| `05_aisuggest.zsh` 內嵌 AI ghost-text | ZLE widget + `region_highlight` | bash readline 沒有 ghost-text 介面，只能改成「按鍵→替換 buffer」，沒有預覽 |
| `04_ai_capture.zsh` 鍵綁 | `zle -N` + `bindkey -M viins` | `bind -x` 能做但回不了 buffer，只能 `READLINE_LINE`/`READLINE_POINT` 暴力寫，UX 大幅下降 |
| `11_tools_picker.zsh` / `12_television.zsh` / `22_sesh.zsh` 的 Alt+T/R/P/G/E/A/I/S | `bindkey` + ZLE | 改 `bind -x` 可動但寫法重做 |
| zsh-autosuggestions、zsh-syntax-highlighting、zsh-vi-mode | OMZ 插件 | bash 對應品質差很多（`ble.sh` 是最接近的，但又是另一個依賴 + 跟 bash-preexec 衝突） |
| Oh-My-Zsh git plugin 的 `gca` / `gcam!` 等簡寫 | OMZ | 要全部自己寫 alias |
| `${PWD//\//-}`、`${m:t}`、glob qualifier、`read -q`、`emulate -L zsh`、`local_options null_glob`、`zparseopts` | zsh 內建 | 全部要改寫；`read -q` → `read -n 1`、`:t` → `basename`、null_glob → `shopt -s nullglob`（bash 4+）、`zparseopts` → `getopts` 或手刻 |
| `compdef` / `fpath` / OMZ completions | zsh compsys | 要重寫成 `complete`/bash-completion |
| `dot_zshrc.tmpl` 的 `zvm_after_init` 重綁 fzf | zsh-vi-mode hook | 沒這個 hook 問題 |

`claude-plans-here` 那種長函式裡 `read -q`、`${m:t}`、`null_glob`、`(N)` glob 、`{groot//\//-}` 全部要改，可改但相當瑣碎。

## 建議方向（如果真的要做）

我的建議是**不要走「雙支援」這條，除非有具體場景需要**。理由：

1. 你 bootstrap 流程（ansible / chezmoi）本來就在每台機器裝 zsh，沒有「只能用 bash」的固定環境。
2. 真正的 portability 痛點是 **登入別人的機器**（jump host、container、SSH 過去做事）— 這個用 `kiss-my-zsh`/`zsh -c`/把 zsh 帶進去 比維護兩套 rc 划算。
3. 即便拆成 `shell/` 共用層，30% 的 zsh-only 功能 = 大部分你日常按的鍵，在 bash 模式下就是「半殘」狀態，會養成「不要進 bash」的反射，反而證明拆分沒意義。

如果還是要做，建議的最小化方案：

- 抽 `dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh` + `10_aliases.sh`（POSIX 子集），同時被 zsh / bash 載。
- 寫一支極簡 `dot_bashrc.tmpl`：source 共用層 + starship + fzf + zoxide + mise + atuin（這幾個都有 bash 版），**不嘗試**移植 aisuggest / ai_capture / vi-mode / tools-picker。
- 文件明寫「bash 是 fallback / 維運場景，互動功能請用 zsh」。
- 預期維護成本：共用層 ~100 行 + bashrc ~80 行，不會爆炸；但測試矩陣會 ×2。

要我直接動手做這個最小化拆分嗎？還是你只是先評估、暫不執行？

## oh-my-bash 能補上什麼

對比一下我先前的兩段表：

| 部分 completion 機制 | ✅ 有自己的 completions/ 目錄管理 |
| Theme | ✅ 有 themes（但我們用 starship，不需要） |

也就是說，**「OMZ-like 開發者體驗」這層 oh-my-bash 給得起**。如果只看 `dot_zshrc.tmpl` 上半段（`plugins=(git zsh-autosuggestions ...)` 那段），確實可以對著抄一份 `dot_bashrc.tmpl`。

## oh-my-bash 仍然解決不了的（重點）

這些不是 OMZ 框架問題，而是 **bash readline 本身的限制**，oh-my-bash 是套在 readline 上的薄殼，無法繞過：

| 功能 | bash readline 能做到的程度 | 差距 |
|---|---|---|
| `aisuggest` 內嵌 AI ghost-text | ❌ readline 無 ghost-text rendering API | 完全做不到，要靠 **ble.sh** 重寫 |
| zsh-autosuggestions（fish 風格灰字補全） | ❌ readline 沒有預覽機制 | 同上，需 ble.sh |
| zsh-syntax-highlighting（即時染色） | ❌ readline 不重繪 buffer | 同上，需 ble.sh |
| zsh-vi-mode 的 surround / text-object | ⚠️ `set -o vi` 只有最基本動作 | oh-my-bash 的 vi-mode plugin 做不到那個層級 |
| ZLE widget（`zle -N`、`widgets[aisuggest]`） | ⚠️ 只能用 `bind -x` + `READLINE_LINE` 改 buffer | tools-picker / television / sesh 要改寫，UX 退化 |
| `read -q`、`${m:t}`、glob qualifier、`zparseopts` | ❌ 都要改寫 | 跟有沒有 oh-my-bash 無關 |

差距的 80% 集中在「buffer 即時渲染」這件事，**只有 ble.sh 補得上**。oh-my-bash 文件自己也建議搭 ble.sh 才能達到接近 zsh 的體驗。

## 加上 ble.sh 後的真實成本

如果走 **oh-my-bash + ble.sh** 全套：

- ✅ 能做出接近 zsh 的互動體驗（autosuggest / 高亮 / vi-mode）
- ⚠️ ble.sh 是一個 ~3 萬行 awk-in-bash 的大專案，啟動慢（典型 200-500ms vs. 你 zsh 已優化過的水準），和 bash-preexec、starship、direnv 偶爾打架，hook 順序敏感
- ⚠️ aisuggest / ai_capture 要從 `zle -N` 改寫成 `ble-bind -x`，雖然 ble.sh 的 widget 模型很像 ZLE，但 API 名字、quote 語意、區域高亮 (`region_highlight` vs ble.sh 的 `_ble_edit_str`) 全都要逐個對照
- ⚠️ ble.sh + oh-my-bash 的相容性是「大致 OK 但會踩雷」，oh-my-bash issue tracker 有不少這類報告
- ⚠️ 維護矩陣：zsh / bash+omb / bash+omb+ble / 純 bash fallback —— 變四種組合，CI 顧不到

## 修正後的建議

如果之前我給 5/10，oh-my-bash 把分數從 5 推到 6——**還沒到推薦做的門檻**。

具體方案優先級（由划算到不划算）：

1. **不做雙支援**，bootstrap 確保有 zsh 即可（現狀）。
2. **抽 `dot_config/shell/` 共用層**（env/alias 的 POSIX 子集），給維運場景用 `bash --rcfile` 臨時跳板，不追求完整 UX。
3. **加 oh-my-bash 但不加 ble.sh**：做出來是個「好像 OMZ 但每次按 Tab 都會想念 zsh」的半殘版，不建議。
4. **完整 oh-my-bash + ble.sh + 重寫 aisuggest**：技術上做得到，但維護成本翻倍，且 ble.sh 的穩定性會讓你日常被打斷。**強烈不建議**，除非有「必須在 bash 環境提供完整 UX」的具體場景（例如：要在某些公司管的機器，policy 禁裝 zsh）。

我傾向選 **方案 1**，必要時做 **方案 2**。要走 2 的話我可以動手——把 PATH/export/Homebrew shellenv/GFW mirror/GOPATH/BUN_INSTALL/通用 alias 抽到 `dot_config/shell/`，zsh 和 bash 都 source，bashrc 額外接 starship+fzf+zoxide+mise+atuin。範圍大概 150 行新增、~30 行從 zsh 那邊改成 source 共用層。

你想走 1 還是 2？

3	# Implied parent dirs of managed files / externals (e.g. ~/.local when only
4	# ~/.local/share/toolkami/toolkami.rb is managed) inherit mode from
5	# `0o777 & ~umask`. Default umask is the user's login umask, which on macOS
6	# (002 → 0775) and various Linux distros (022 → 0755 / 0700 for ~) differs,
7	# producing recurring "mode-only diff" noise on .local and friends across
8	# the fleet. Pin umask to 022 so implied dirs are always 0755 regardless of
9	# host login umask. Files that need stricter modes use the `private_` prefix
10	# explicitly.
11	umask = 0o022

2	# /// script
3	# requires-python = ">=3.11"

10	"""
11	dotfiles_init.py — Interactive wrapper around `chezmoi init` inspired by
12	Vercel Labs' `skills` CLI (https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills).
13	
14	The existing `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` defines ~19 prompts (profile, email, name,
15	16 feature flags). `chezmoi init` asks them sequentially, which works but
16	hides the feature flags from each other and makes "set up a new machine
17	the way I always do" a manual checklist. This wrapper:
18	
19	  1. Pre-flights chezmoi / git / SSH key and offers to fix gaps.
20	  2. Lets you pick a pre-configured BUNDLE (personal-mac, work-mac,
21	     server-linux, minimal) that ticks typical feature flags for you.
22	  3. Presents feature flags grouped, as a questionary multi-select you can
23	     fly through with Space + Enter.
24	  4. Shells out to `chezmoi init <repo> --apply [--ssh] --promptString ... `
25	     so chezmoi remains the source of truth — we just pre-answer its prompts.
26	  5. Streams chezmoi's output live and prints a recap at the end.
27	
28	The wrapper also has a `doctor` subcommand that greps `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`
29	and `Dockerfile` and fails loudly if any prompt key in those files is
30	missing from this script's PROMPTS list (or vice versa). Run it in CI / a
31	pre-commit hook to catch drift — per CLAUDE.md's "Dockerfile" cross-file
32	rule, adding a chezmoi prompt means updating three files in one commit.
33	
34	Invocation:
35	    # Fresh machine (via bootstrap.sh which installs uv first):
36	    curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | bash
37	
38	    # Existing chezmoi source dir — re-apply with new answers:
39	    uv run --script ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py
40	
41	    # Schema parity check:
42	    uv run --script ~/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py doctor
43	"""
44	from __future__ import annotations
45

309	@dataclass
310	class Preflight:
311	    chezmoi: str | None
312	    git: str | None
313	    ssh_hint: str | None                # how we detected SSH is ready (or None)
314	    source_exists: bool
315	    os_name: str
316	    is_tty: bool
317	
318	
319	def _detect_ssh() -> str | None:
320	    """Return a short hint describing why we think SSH-to-github is configured,
321	    or None if we can't tell. We accept several signals because the user may
322	    keep keys under non-canonical names and route them via ~/.ssh/config or
323	    its Include'd fragments."""
324	    # (1) Canonical default keys.
325	    for k in SSH_DEFAULT_KEYS:
326	        if k.exists():
327	            return f"default key at {k}"
328	    # (2) ~/.ssh/config (or an Include'd file under ~/.ssh/config.d/) with a
329	    # `Host github…` stanza → user is routing a custom key.
330	    config_texts: list[str] = []
331	    for root in (SSH_CONFIG, *((SSH_DIR / "config.d").glob("*") if (SSH_DIR / "config.d").is_dir() else ())):
332	        if root.is_file():
333	            try:
334	                config_texts.append(root.read_text(errors="replace"))
335	            except OSError:
336	                pass
337	    joined = "\n".join(config_texts)
338	    if re.search(r"(?mi)^\s*Host\s+[\w.\-\* ]*github", joined):
339	        return "~/.ssh/config routes github.com"
340	    # (3) Any loaded key in the agent (default or via IdentityAgent socket).
341	    try:
342	        r = subprocess.run(["ssh-add", "-l"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=3)
343	        if r.returncode == 0 and r.stdout.strip():
344	            return "ssh-agent has keys loaded"
345	    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
346	        pass
347	    return None
348	
349	
350	def detect() -> Preflight:
351	    import platform
352	    return Preflight(
353	        chezmoi=shutil.which("chezmoi"),
354	        git=shutil.which("git"),
355	        ssh_hint=_detect_ssh(),
356	        source_exists=(CHEZMOI_SOURCE_DIR / ".git").is_dir(),
357	        os_name={"Darwin": "darwin", "Linux": "linux"}.get(platform.system(), platform.system().lower()),
358	        is_tty=sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty(),
359	    )

373	def install_chezmoi_interactive(os_name: str) -> str:
374	    """Offer to install chezmoi via the canonical one-liner; return new path."""
375	    if not questionary.confirm("chezmoi not found. Install via get.chezmoi.io/lb?", default=True).ask():
376	        console.print("[red]chezmoi is required; aborting.[/red]")
377	        sys.exit(1)
378	    target = Path.home() / ".local" / "bin"
379	    target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
380	    subprocess.check_call(
381	        "curl -fsLS --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 get.chezmoi.io/lb | sh",
382	        shell=True,
383	        env={**os.environ, "BINDIR": str(target)},
384	    )
385	    path = shutil.which("chezmoi") or str(target / "chezmoi")
386	    console.print(f"[green]chezmoi installed at {path}[/green]\n")
387	    return path

390	def ensure_ssh_key_interactive() -> Path | None:
391	    """Offer to generate an ed25519 key; return path or None if user declined."""
392	    if not questionary.confirm(
393	        "No SSH key found. Generate ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 for GitHub (SSH clone)?",
394	        default=True,
395	    ).ask():
396	        return None
397	    key_path = Path.home() / ".ssh" / "id_ed25519"
398	    key_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)
399	    email = questionary.text(
400	        "Email to tag the SSH key with:",
401	        default="daviddwlee84@gmail.com",
402	    ).ask() or "daviddwlee84@gmail.com"
403	    subprocess.check_call(["ssh-keygen", "-t", "ed25519", "-C", email, "-f", str(key_path), "-N", ""])
404	    pub = key_path.with_suffix(".pub").read_text().strip()
405	    console.print(Panel(
406	        f"[bold]Add this public key to GitHub → Settings → SSH keys:[/bold]\n\n{pub}\n\n"
407	        f"Open: https://github.com/settings/ssh/new",
408	        title="SSH key generated",
409	        border_style="green",
410	    ))
411	    questionary.press_any_key_to_continue("Press any key once you've added the key to GitHub...").ask()
412	    return key_path

440	def ask_basics(pf: Preflight, overrides: dict[str, object]) -> dict[str, object]:
441	    # profile: auto-detect on Darwin; ask ubuntu_desktop vs ubuntu_server on Linux
442	    default_profile = "macos" if pf.os_name == "darwin" else "ubuntu_server"
443	    if pf.os_name == "darwin":
444	        profile = "macos"
445	        console.print(f"[dim]profile → {profile} (auto-detected)[/dim]")
446	    else:
447	        profile = questionary.select(
448	            "Which profile?",
449	            choices=["ubuntu_server", "ubuntu_desktop"],
450	            default=overrides.get("profile", default_profile),
451	        ).ask() or default_profile
452	
453	    name = questionary.text(
454	        "Your full name:",
455	        default=str(overrides.get("name", _default_for("name"))),
456	    ).ask() or _default_for("name")
457	
458	    email = questionary.text(
459	        "Your git email:",
460	        default=str(overrides.get("email", _default_for("email"))),
461	    ).ask() or _default_for("email")
462	
463	    return {"profile": profile, "name": name, "email": email}

466	def resolve_basics_non_interactive(
467	    pf: Preflight,
468	    overrides: dict[str, object],
469	    *,
470	    name_flag: str | None,
471	    email_flag: str | None,
472	    profile_flag: str | None,
473	) -> dict[str, object]:
474	    """Non-interactive basics: flag → bundle override → embedded default → OS auto-detect."""
475	    if profile_flag:
476	        profile = profile_flag
477	    elif "profile" in overrides:
478	        profile = overrides["profile"]
479	    else:
480	        profile = "macos" if pf.os_name == "darwin" else "ubuntu_server"
481	    name = name_flag or overrides.get("name") or _default_for("name")
482	    email = email_flag or overrides.get("email") or _default_for("email")
483	    return {"profile": profile, "name": name, "email": email}

486	def resolve_features_non_interactive(pf: Preflight, overrides: dict[str, object]) -> dict[str, bool]:
487	    """Non-interactive features: bundle override → embedded default, skipping darwin-only on Linux."""
488	    result: dict[str, bool] = {}
489	    for p in PROMPTS:
490	        if p.kind != "bool" or p.hidden:
491	            continue
492	        if p.darwin_only and pf.os_name != "darwin":
493	            continue
494	        result[p.key] = bool(overrides.get(p.key, p.default))
495	    return result

497	
498	def ask_features(pf: Preflight, overrides: dict[str, object]) -> dict[str, bool]:
499	    """Grouped multi-select. Returns {key: bool} for every non-basics bool prompt."""
500	    feature_prompts = [p for p in PROMPTS if p.kind == "bool" and not p.hidden
501	                       and (pf.os_name == "darwin" or not p.darwin_only)]
502	
503	    groups: dict[str, list[Prompt]] = {}
504	    for p in feature_prompts:
505	        groups.setdefault(p.group, []).append(p)
506	
507	    # Build one flat checkbox preserving group order, with group headers as
508	    # disabled separator rows (purely visual).
509	    choices: list[questionary.Choice] = []
510	    for group, prompts in groups.items():
511	        choices.append(questionary.Separator(f"── {group} ──"))
512	        for p in prompts:
513	            initial = overrides.get(p.key, p.default)
514	            choices.append(questionary.Choice(
515	                title=f"{p.label}  — {p.desc}",
516	                value=p.key,
517	                checked=bool(initial),
518	            ))
519	
520	    console.print()
521	    console.print("[bold]Feature flags[/bold] — Space to toggle, ↑/↓ to move, Enter to confirm.")
522	    selected_keys = questionary.checkbox(
523	        "Which features?",
524	        choices=choices,
525	    ).ask() or []
526	
527	    result: dict[str, bool] = {}
528	    for p in feature_prompts:
529	        result[p.key] = p.key in selected_keys
530	    return result

534	    t = Table(title="Answers", show_header=False, box=None, padding=(0, 2))
535	    t.add_column("Key", style="cyan"); t.add_column("Value")
536	    for p in PROMPTS:

538	            continue

540	        style = "green" if val is True else ("dim" if val is False else "")
541	        t.add_row(p.key, f"[{style}]{val}[/{style}]" if style else str(val))
542	    console.print(t)
543	    console.print()
544	    console.print(Panel(

548	    ))

552	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
553	# Runner
554	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
555	
556	def build_chezmoi_argv(
557	    answers: dict[str, object],
558	    *,
559	    chezmoi_bin: str,
560	    repo: str | None,
561	    use_ssh: bool,
562	    apply: bool,
563	    darwin: bool,
564	) -> list[str]:
565	    """Build the chezmoi init argv. The critical detail is that `chezmoi init`
566	    matches --promptBool / --promptString / --promptChoice flags by the PROMPT
567	    TEXT (3rd arg to promptXOnce in the template), NOT the key name. That's
568	    why every Prompt carries a prompt_text field and we use it here as the
569	    flag key."""
570	    argv: list[str] = [chezmoi_bin, "init"]
571	    if repo:
572	        argv.append(repo)
573	    if use_ssh:
574	        argv.append("--ssh")
575	    if apply:
576	        argv.append("--apply")
577	    by_key = {p.key: p for p in PROMPTS}
578	    # String + choice prompts (basics).
579	    for key in ("email", "name"):
580	        if key in answers:
581	            argv += ["--promptString", f"{by_key[key].prompt_text}={answers[key]}"]
582	    if "profile" in answers:
583	        argv += ["--promptChoice", f"{by_key['profile'].prompt_text}={answers['profile']}"]
584	    # Non-basics choice prompts (e.g. discordChannel).
585	    for p in PROMPTS:
586	        if p.kind != "choice" or p.hidden:
587	            continue
588	        if p.darwin_only and not darwin:
589	            continue
590	        if p.key not in answers:
591	            continue
592	        argv += ["--promptChoice", f"{p.prompt_text}={answers[p.key]}"]
593	    # Bool prompts — skip darwin-only on linux (chezmoi never evaluates them there).
594	    for p in PROMPTS:
595	        if p.kind != "bool" or p.hidden:
596	            continue
597	        if p.darwin_only and not darwin:
598	            continue
599	        if p.key not in answers:
600	            continue
601	        val_str = "true" if answers[p.key] else "false"
602	        argv += ["--promptBool", f"{p.prompt_text}={val_str}"]
603	    return argv
604	
605	
606	def run_chezmoi(argv: list[str]) -> int:
607	    console.print(f"[dim]$ {' '.join(argv)}[/dim]")
608	    console.rule("[bold]chezmoi output[/bold]")
609	    rc = subprocess.call(argv)
610	    console.rule()
611	    return rc
612

616	    panel_body = (
617	        f"{'✓' if rc == 0 else '✗'} chezmoi init exit={rc}\n"
618	        f"✓ {len(enabled)} of {sum(1 for p in PROMPTS if p.kind == 'bool' and not p.hidden)} feature groups enabled\n"
619	        f"\nEnabled:\n  " + ("\n  ".join(enabled) if enabled else "(none)")
620	        + "\n\nNext:\n  • Review with: chezmoi diff\n"
621	          "  • Upgrade later with: just upgrade-all\n"
622	          "  • Fleet-apply to other hosts with: just fleet-apply"
623	    )
624	    console.print(Panel(
625	        panel_body,
626	        title="Summary",
627	        border_style="green" if rc == 0 else "red",
628	    ))

631	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
632	# Doctor: schema parity check
633	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
634	
635	def doctor_scan(source_dir: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, str], set[str], dict[str, str]]:
636	    """Return (tmpl: {key: prompt_text}, dockerfile_keys, script: {key: prompt_text})."""
637	    tmpl = (source_dir / ".chezmoi.toml.tmpl").read_text()
638	    tmpl_pairs: dict[str, str] = {}
639	    for k, txt in re.findall(
640	        r'prompt(?:String|Bool|Choice)Once\s+\.\s+"(\w+)"\s+"([^"]+)"', tmpl):
641	        tmpl_pairs[k] = txt
642	
643	    dockerfile = (source_dir / "Dockerfile").read_text()
644	    def _arg_to_camel(s: str) -> str:
645	        parts = s.lower().split("_")
646	        return parts[0] + "".join(p.title() for p in parts[1:])
647	    docker_args = re.findall(r"ARG\s+CHEZMOI_(\w+)\s*=", dockerfile)
648	    docker_keys = {_arg_to_camel(a) for a in docker_args if a.lower() != "repo"}
649	
650	    script_pairs = {p.key: p.prompt_text for p in PROMPTS}
651	    return tmpl_pairs, docker_keys, script_pairs
652	
653	
654	def doctor_report(source_dir: Path) -> int:
655	    tmpl, docker, script = doctor_scan(source_dir)
656	    all_keys = set(tmpl) | docker | set(script)
657	
658	    rows = []
659	    drift = False
660	    for k in sorted(all_keys):
661	        in_t = "✓" if k in tmpl else "[red]✗[/red]"
662	        in_d = "✓" if k in docker else "[yellow]✗[/yellow]"
663	        in_s = "✓" if k in script else "[red]✗[/red]"
664	        if not (k in tmpl and k in docker and k in script):
665	            drift = True
666	        text_note = ""
667	        # Prompt-text mismatches are critical — chezmoi init matches on the text.
668	        if k in tmpl and k in script and tmpl[k] != script[k]:
669	            drift = True
670	            text_note = f"[red]text mismatch[/red]"
671	        rows.append((k, in_t, in_d, in_s, text_note))
672	
673	    t = Table(title="Prompt schema parity")
674	    t.add_column("key"); t.add_column(".chezmoi.toml.tmpl")
675	    t.add_column("Dockerfile"); t.add_column("dotfiles_init.py")
676	    t.add_column("notes")
677	    for row in rows:
678	        t.add_row(*row)
679	    console.print(t)
680	
681	    if drift:
682	        console.print("[red]Drift detected — update the missing files so all three agree.[/red]")
683	        console.print("[dim]Prompt-text mismatches are especially important — chezmoi init\n"
684	                      "matches --promptBool flags by the full prompt text, not the key.[/dim]")
685	        return 1
686	    console.print("[green]All three surfaces agree (keys + prompt texts).[/green]")
687	    return 0
688

694	def _default_for(key: str) -> object:
695	    for p in PROMPTS:
696	        if p.key == key:
697	            return p.default
698	    raise KeyError(key)

701	@dataclass
702	class InitCmd:
703	    """Interactive wrapper around `chezmoi init`.
704	
705	    With --yes (and optionally --bundle / --name / --email / --profile) the
706	    flow becomes fully non-interactive: no TTY required, no prompts shown.
707	    Suitable for Docker / CI. Missing basics fall back to bundle overrides,
708	    then embedded defaults, then OS auto-detection for profile."""
709	
710	    repo: Annotated[str, tyro.conf.arg(help="Chezmoi repo arg (omit on re-init)")] = DEFAULT_REPO
711	    bundle: Annotated[str | None, tyro.conf.arg(help="Skip the picker; use this bundle")] = None
712	    name: Annotated[str | None, tyro.conf.arg(help="Git full name (non-interactive override)")] = None
713	    email: Annotated[str | None, tyro.conf.arg(help="Git email (non-interactive override)")] = None
714	    profile: Annotated[str | None, tyro.conf.arg(help="Profile: macos|ubuntu_desktop|ubuntu_server (auto-detected if omitted)")] = None
715	    ssh: Annotated[bool, tyro.conf.arg(help="Force --ssh even if no key is present")] = False
716	    yes: Annotated[bool, tyro.conf.arg(help="Fully non-interactive: no prompts, no confirmation, assume defaults")] = False
717	    dry_run: Annotated[bool, tyro.conf.arg(help="Print the chezmoi command instead of running it")] = False

736	    | Annotated[ListBundlesCmd, tyro.conf.subcommand(name="list-bundles")]
737	)

739	
740	def run_init(cmd: InitCmd) -> int:
741	    pf = detect()
742	    print_preflight(pf)
743	
744	    # TTY is only required for interactive mode. --yes / --dry-run don't need one.
745	    if not cmd.yes and not cmd.dry_run and not pf.is_tty:
746	        console.print("[red]No TTY detected — cannot run interactive prompts.\n"
747	                      "If you piped this from curl, re-exec with `</dev/tty`.\n"
748	                      "For non-interactive use, pass --yes (and optionally --bundle / --name / --email / --profile).[/red]")
749	        return 2
750	
751	    # Ensure chezmoi
752	    if pf.chezmoi:
753	        chezmoi_bin = pf.chezmoi
754	    elif cmd.yes:
755	        console.print("[yellow]chezmoi not found; installing silently...[/yellow]")
756	        chezmoi_bin = _install_chezmoi_silent()
757	    else:
758	        chezmoi_bin = install_chezmoi_interactive(pf.os_name)
759	
760	    # Ensure ssh key (only matters for fresh init with --ssh clone)
761	    use_ssh = cmd.ssh or bool(pf.ssh_hint)
762	    if not pf.source_exists and use_ssh and not pf.ssh_hint:
763	        if cmd.yes:
764	            use_ssh = False  # silent HTTPS fallback in non-interactive mode
765	            console.print("[yellow]No SSH key; using HTTPS clone (non-interactive).[/yellow]")
766	        else:
767	            key = ensure_ssh_key_interactive()
768	            if key is None:
769	                use_ssh = False
770	                console.print("[yellow]Falling back to HTTPS clone (no SSH key).[/yellow]")
771	
772	    # Bundle: flag → picker → default "minimal" under --yes (Docker/CI)
773	    if cmd.bundle:
774	        bundle_name = cmd.bundle
775	    elif cmd.yes:
776	        bundle_name = "minimal"
777	    else:
778	        bundle_name = ask_bundle()
779	    if bundle_name not in BUNDLES:
780	        console.print(f"[red]Unknown bundle: {bundle_name}[/red]")
781	        return 2
782	    overrides = dict(BUNDLES[bundle_name])
783	    console.print(f"[dim]Bundle: {bundle_name}[/dim]\n")
784	
785	    # Basics & features — interactive prompts vs pure resolution.
786	    if cmd.yes:
787	        basics = resolve_basics_non_interactive(
788	            pf, overrides,
789	            name_flag=cmd.name, email_flag=cmd.email, profile_flag=cmd.profile,
790	        )
791	        features = resolve_features_non_interactive(pf, overrides)
792	    else:
793	        basics = ask_basics(pf, overrides)
794	        features = ask_features(pf, overrides)
795	
796	    answers: dict[str, object] = {**basics, **features}
797	
798	    argv = build_chezmoi_argv(
799	        answers,
800	        chezmoi_bin=chezmoi_bin,
801	        repo=None if pf.source_exists else cmd.repo,
802	        use_ssh=use_ssh,
803	        apply=not cmd.no_apply,
804	        darwin=(pf.os_name == "darwin"),
805	    )
806	
807	    if not cmd.yes and not confirm_plan(answers, argv):
808	        console.print("[yellow]Aborted.[/yellow]")
809	        return 130
810	
811	    if cmd.dry_run:
812	        console.print(Panel(" ".join(argv), title="dry-run", border_style="yellow"))
813	        return 0
814	
815	    rc = run_chezmoi(argv)
816	    print_recap(answers, rc)
817	    return rc
818	
819	
820	def _install_chezmoi_silent() -> str:
821	    """Non-interactive chezmoi install; same one-liner as install_chezmoi_interactive."""
822	    target = Path.home() / ".local" / "bin"
823	    target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
824	    subprocess.check_call(
825	        "curl -fsLS --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 get.chezmoi.io/lb | sh",
826	        shell=True,
827	        env={**os.environ, "BINDIR": str(target)},
828	    )
829	    return shutil.which("chezmoi") or str(target / "chezmoi")
830	
831	
832	def run_doctor(cmd: DoctorCmd) -> int:
833	    if not cmd.source.exists():
834	        console.print(f"[red]Source dir not found: {cmd.source}[/red]")
835	        return 2
836	    return doctor_report(cmd.source)
837	
838	
839	def run_list_bundles(cmd: ListBundlesCmd) -> int:  # noqa: ARG001
840	    for name, overrides in BUNDLES.items():
841	        t = Table(title=name, show_header=False, box=None, padding=(0, 2))
842	        t.add_column(style="cyan"); t.add_column()
843	        for p in PROMPTS:
844	            if p.hidden or p.kind != "bool":
845	                continue
846	            v = overrides.get(p.key, p.default)
847	            origin = "(bundle)" if p.key in overrides else "(default)"
848	            t.add_row(p.key, f"{v} [dim]{origin}[/dim]")
849	        console.print(t); console.print()
850	    return 0
851	
852	
853	def main() -> int:
854	    cmd = tyro.cli(Command, default=InitCmd())
855	    if isinstance(cmd, InitCmd):
856	        return run_init(cmd)
857	    if isinstance(cmd, DoctorCmd):
858	        return run_doctor(cmd)
859	    if isinstance(cmd, ListBundlesCmd):
860	        return run_list_bundles(cmd)
861	    return 2

```text
1	# Dotfiles test/devbox container — CentOS 7 (legacy glibc-2.17 corporate target)
2	# Build: docker build -f Dockerfile.centos7 -t dotfiles:centos7 .
3	# Run:   docker run -it dotfiles:centos7
4	#
5	# Closest reproduction of the real-world centos_server target — corporate
6	# data-center boxes still on CentOS Linux 7.9, often noRoot. Validates the
7	# user-level GitHub-release fallback paths documented in
8	# pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md (gate broadening: os_family in
9	# ["Debian", "RedHat"]) and the bootstrap's `uv tool install --python 3.13
10	# ansible-core` Python pin (CentOS 7 ships Python 3.6.8 system-wide).
11	#
12	# CentOS 7 EOL'd 2024-06-30. The base image's default repos point at
13	# mirror.centos.org which now returns 404. Redirect to vault.centos.org
14	# at the very top of the RUN chain — BEFORE any `yum install`.
15	
16	FROM centos:7
17	
18	# Build arguments for chezmoi configuration
19	ARG CHEZMOI_PROFILE=centos_server
20	ARG CHEZMOI_EMAIL=docker@example.com
21	ARG CHEZMOI_NAME="Docker User"
22	ARG CHEZMOI_USE_CHINESE_MIRROR=false
23	ARG CHEZMOI_GITLEAKS_ALL_REPOS=false
24	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_CODING_AGENTS=false
25	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_BITWARDEN=false
26	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_PYTHON_UV_TOOLS=false
27	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_JS_CLI_TOOLS=false
28	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_LLM_TOOLS=false
29	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_AI_DESKTOP_APPS=false
30	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_BREW_APPS=false
31	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_INPUT_METHOD=false
32	ARG CHEZMOI_DISCORD_CHANNEL=none
33	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_NETWORKING_TOOLS=false
34	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_IAC_TOOLS=false
35	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_MEDIA_TOOLS=false
36	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_DOTNET_TOOLS=false
37	ARG CHEZMOI_NO_ROOT=false
38	ARG CHEZMOI_BACKUP_MODE=off
39	ARG CHEZMOI_ALLOW_PARTIAL_FAILURE=true
40	ARG CHEZMOI_MOTD_STYLE=figlet
41	ARG CHEZMOI_REPO=daviddwlee84
42	
43	# Redirect default repos to vault.centos.org (post-EOL archive). Must run
44	# before the first yum invocation; otherwise mirrorlist.centos.org returns
45	# 404 and the layer collapses immediately.
46	RUN sed -i 's|^mirrorlist=|#mirrorlist=|g' /etc/yum.repos.d/CentOS-*.repo \
47	    && sed -i 's|^#baseurl=http://mirror.centos.org|baseurl=http://vault.centos.org|g' /etc/yum.repos.d/CentOS-*.repo
48	
49	# Install minimal dependencies.
50	# python3 here is CentOS 7's 3.6.8; chezmoi bootstrap pins ansible to

40

45	  register: current_shell_macos
46	  changed_when: false
47	  check_mode: false
48	  failed_when: false
49	
50	- name: Get current login shell (Linux)
51	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] != "Darwin"
52	  ansible.builtin.command:
53	    cmd: "getent passwd {{ ansible_facts['user_id'] }}"
54	  register: current_shell_linux

61	    current_login_shell: >-
62	      {{ (current_shell_macos.stdout | default('')).split()[-1]

```text
1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Bootstrap script - installs Homebrew, uv, ansible, mise, and galaxy collections
3	# Runs BEFORE any ansible playbooks
4	# Profile: {{ .profile }}
5	
6	set -e
7	
8	# Colors for output
9	RED='\033[0;31m'
10	GREEN='\033[0;32m'
11	YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
12	BLUE='\033[0;34m'
13	NC='\033[0m' # No Color
14	
15	info() {
16	    echo -e "${BLUE}[INFO]${NC} $1"
17	}
18	
19	success() {
20	    echo -e "${GREEN}[SUCCESS]${NC} $1"
21	}
22	
23	warn() {
24	    echo -e "${YELLOW}[WARN]${NC} $1"
25	}
26	
27	error() {
28	    echo -e "${RED}[ERROR]${NC} $1"
29	}
30	
31	# Fix broken locale (e.g. RPi with LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 but locale not generated)
32	# Ansible requires UTF-8 encoding, so fall back to C.UTF-8 (not plain C).
33	if locale 2>&1 | grep -qi "cannot set"; then
34	    warn "Broken locale detected, falling back to LC_ALL=C.UTF-8"
35	    export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
36	    export LANG=C.UTF-8
37	fi
38	
39	# Ensure PATH includes local bin and Homebrew
40	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
41	
42	# --- Shared sudo session (prompt once, reuse across bootstrap + ansible + brew)
43	# Inlined from scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh via chezmoi's `include` so the helper
44	# travels with the rendered script (no runtime path lookup back to the source
45	# tree). See that file for API, lifetime, and clean-up guarantees.
46	{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}
47	# --- end sudo helper
48	
49	# Decide at render time whether *any* script in the apply flow will need sudo.
50	# If not, we never prompt, never create the state dir, never spawn a watchdog.
51	# Conditions mirror the sudo surfaces in every run-script:
52	#   - Linux, non-noRoot: bootstrap apt-get + ansible become tasks.
53	#   - macOS, installBrewApps: pkg-based cask installers (google-drive, etc.).
54	#   - macOS, installInputMethod: Squirrel cask pkg installer (ansible).
55	NEED_SUDO={{ if or (and (eq .chezmoi.os "linux") (not .noRoot)) (and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (or .installBrewApps .installInputMethod)) }}1{{ else }}0{{ end }}
56	
57	# Set up the shared sudo session FIRST so bootstrap's own `apt-get` lines (and
58	# every later run-script) reuse the same cached credential. Trap INT/TERM/HUP
59	# only — no EXIT trap, because the next run-script needs the state to survive
60	# this process exiting. End-of-flow cleanup is done by the detached watchdog
61	# (see sudo_shared.sh).
62	if [[ "$NEED_SUDO" == "1" ]]; then
63	    if ! sudo_session_init "bootstrap"; then
64	        warn "Could not establish a sudo session (no TTY and sudo needs a password);"
65	        warn "bootstrap will attempt its sudo steps anyway and they may prompt or skip."
66	    fi
67	fi
68	
69	{{ if .useChineseMirror -}}
70	# GFW mirrors (useChineseMirror=true). Must be set BEFORE the first
71	# `brew install`, `rustup`, or `mise install` so every bootstrap fetch
72	# goes through the mirror instead of the blocked upstream.
73	# Homebrew mirrors (ordered by typical reliability behind GFW):
74	#   - Aliyun (ACTIVE): commercial CDN, least queueing
75	#       https://developer.aliyun.com/mirror/homebrew
76	#   - USTC:  university mirror, low queueing; path is top-level (no /git/homebrew/)
77	#       https://mirrors.ustc.edu.cn/help/brew.git.html
78	#   - BFSU:  mirrors TUNA content but less congested
79	#       https://mirrors.bfsu.edu.cn/help/homebrew-bottles/
80	#   - TUNA:  Tsinghua, upstream of BFSU; frequent "Waiting in queue" on brew.git
81	#       https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/help/homebrew/
82	# Homebrew env vars are single-value — no native fallback. To switch, comment
83	# out the active block and uncomment another.
84	export HOMEBREW_API_DOMAIN="https://mirrors.aliyun.com/homebrew-bottles/api"
85	export HOMEBREW_BOTTLE_DOMAIN="https://mirrors.aliyun.com/homebrew-bottles"
86	export HOMEBREW_BREW_GIT_REMOTE="https://mirrors.aliyun.com/homebrew/brew.git"
87	export HOMEBREW_CORE_GIT_REMOTE="https://mirrors.aliyun.com/homebrew/homebrew-core.git"
88	# USTC alternative:
89	#   export HOMEBREW_API_DOMAIN="https://mirrors.ustc.edu.cn/homebrew-bottles/api"
90	#   export HOMEBREW_BOTTLE_DOMAIN="https://mirrors.ustc.edu.cn/homebrew-bottles"
91	#   export HOMEBREW_BREW_GIT_REMOTE="https://mirrors.ustc.edu.cn/brew.git"
92	#   export HOMEBREW_CORE_GIT_REMOTE="https://mirrors.ustc.edu.cn/homebrew-core.git"
93	# BFSU alternative:

95	#   export HOMEBREW_BOTTLE_DOMAIN="https://mirrors.bfsu.edu.cn/homebrew-bottles"

100	#   export HOMEBREW_BOTTLE_DOMAIN="https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/homebrew-bottles"

1	# Dotfiles test/devbox container — Rocky Linux 9 (modern RHEL-family)
2	# Build: docker build -f Dockerfile.rocky9 -t dotfiles:rocky9 .
3	# Run:   docker run -it dotfiles:rocky9
4	#
5	# Tests the centos_server profile on a current dnf-native distro.
6	# Sister image to Dockerfile.centos7 (which targets the legacy glibc-2.17
7	# corporate scenario). Keep this file's ARG block + devuser + chezmoi
8	# init flag list in lockstep with Dockerfile and Dockerfile.centos7.
9	
10	FROM rockylinux:9
11	
12	# Build arguments for chezmoi configuration
13	ARG CHEZMOI_PROFILE=centos_server
14	ARG CHEZMOI_EMAIL=docker@example.com
15	ARG CHEZMOI_NAME="Docker User"
16	ARG CHEZMOI_USE_CHINESE_MIRROR=false
17	ARG CHEZMOI_GITLEAKS_ALL_REPOS=false
18	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_CODING_AGENTS=false
19	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_BITWARDEN=false
20	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_PYTHON_UV_TOOLS=false
21	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_JS_CLI_TOOLS=false
22	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_LLM_TOOLS=false
23	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_AI_DESKTOP_APPS=false
24	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_BREW_APPS=false
25	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_INPUT_METHOD=false
26	ARG CHEZMOI_DISCORD_CHANNEL=none
27	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_NETWORKING_TOOLS=false
28	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_IAC_TOOLS=false
29	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_MEDIA_TOOLS=false
30	ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_DOTNET_TOOLS=false
31	ARG CHEZMOI_NO_ROOT=false
32	ARG CHEZMOI_BACKUP_MODE=off
33	ARG CHEZMOI_ALLOW_PARTIAL_FAILURE=true
34	ARG CHEZMOI_MOTD_STYLE=figlet
35	ARG CHEZMOI_REPO=daviddwlee84
36	
37	# Install minimal dependencies.
38	# --allowerasing resolves the curl-minimal vs curl conflict that ships in
39	# the rockylinux:9 base layer; without it dnf aborts on package conflict.
40	# python3 is required for ansible to run modules on localhost.
41	RUN dnf install -y --allowerasing \
42	        ca-certificates \
43	        curl \
44	        sudo \
45	        git \
46	        python3 \
47	    && dnf clean all
48	
49	# Create non-root user with sudo access
50	RUN useradd -m -s /bin/bash devuser \
51	    && echo "devuser ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL" >> /etc/sudoers.d/devuser \
52	    && chmod 0440 /etc/sudoers.d/devuser
53	
54	# Copy local dotfiles source into image
55	# This allows testing local changes without pushing to GitHub
56	COPY --chown=devuser:devuser . /tmp/dotfiles-source
57	
58	# Switch to non-root user
59	USER devuser
60	WORKDIR /home/devuser

```text
1	# Dotfiles Repository — Agent Contract
2	
3	Cross-platform dotfiles managed by **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system deps). This file is the agent-facing contract: maintenance rules, hard invariants, and pointers to docs. User-facing intro is in [README.md](README.md).
4	
5	> **Headroom rule**: keep this file under ~30k chars. Push handbook content into `docs/`; keep only edit rules and cross-file invariants here.
6	
7	## Cross-file maintenance rules
8	
9	When you change one of these surfaces, update the listed mirror file in the same commit. These are the rules most often forgotten.
10	
11	### README.md
12	
13	When adding/modifying configurations, update [README.md](README.md):
14	
15	- **New config files** → "What You Get > Config Files" section
16	- **New ansible roles/tools** → "What You Get > Tools" section
17	- **New platforms** → "Supported Platforms" table
18	- **Changed setup steps** → "Quick Setup" section
19	
20	Keep README.md concise and user-focused. Technical details belong here or in `docs/`.
21	
22	### `docs/` + MkDocs site → `mkdocs.yml` nav
23	
24	`docs/` is published to **<https://daviddwlee84.github.io/dotfiles/>** via a MkDocs Material site (auto-deployed by [`.github/workflows/docs.yml`](.github/workflows/docs.yml) on push-to-main when `docs/**`, `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, or `uv.lock` changes). Source of truth remains the `.md` files in the repo; the site is a renderer.
25	
26	Any time you **add a new `docs/**/*.md` file**:
27	
28	1. Add a nav entry in [`mkdocs.yml`](mkdocs.yml) under the matching top-level section (Tools / Zsh / Neovim / This Repo / Infrastructure / Tutorials / Input methods / Misc). Alphabetical within a section unless there's a narrative order.
29	2. Cross-link from related pages if applicable (e.g., a new `docs/tools/foo.md` probably wants a mention in `docs/tools/tmux/README.md` or `docs/tools/sesh.md` if relevant).
30	3. Run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` locally to catch broken links / stale anchors. If you're adding *external*-relative links (to `dot_config/…`, `pitfalls/…`, `backlog/…`), the `validation.links.not_found: info` config tolerates them — that's intentional, don't tighten it without cleaning up the ~20 known anchor-drift cases tracked in [`backlog/mkdocs-anchor-drift.md`](backlog/mkdocs-anchor-drift.md) first.
31	
32	The `.claude/skills/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh` helper can create a new page + insert the nav entry in one shot, but hand-editing `mkdocs.yml` is also fine as long as strict build passes.
33	
34	**What does NOT belong in `docs/`** (stays at repo root, NOT in MkDocs nav):
35	
36	| Surface | Why |
37	|---|---|
38	| `README.md` | Canonical GitHub landing page; `docs/index.md` links to it (no duplication, no snippet copy) |
39	| `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `GEMINI.md` | Agent-operational contract; `docs/for-maintainers.md` references it |
40	| `TODO.md`, `backlog/`, `pitfalls/` | Dynamic maintainer surfaces; `docs/for-maintainers.md` references them via absolute GitHub URLs (reference, not copy) |
41	| `NOTES.md` | User's personal WIP notes |
42	
43	All four categories are **referenced** from [`docs/for-maintainers.md`](docs/for-maintainers.md) via absolute GitHub URLs — do not add them to `mkdocs.yml` nav or include them via `pymdownx.snippets`. The "reference yes, copy no" rule avoids drift between the site and the live repo root.
44	
45	### Custom aliases & shell functions → `docs/zsh/aliases.md`
46	
47	When adding/modifying/removing a custom alias or shell function in any `dot_config/zsh/` file, update [`docs/zsh/aliases.md`](docs/zsh/aliases.md): one row per entry with command name, type (`alias` or `function`), source file (relative to repo root), and a one-line description.
48	
49	### `gui_apps_linux` ansible role → `docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md`
50	
51	When adding/modifying/removing a Linux GUI app in [`dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml`](dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml), update the **Inventory** table in [`docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md`](docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md). The playbook is the single source of truth for the per-app mechanism / auto-update story, and is the first thing a maintainer (or agent) should read before adding a new app — it contains the `.deb` / Snap / Flatpak / AppImage decision tree and the concrete copy-paste patterns. Read it first; update it in the same commit.
52	
53	### Dockerfile + dotfiles_init wrapper
54	
55	When adding new chezmoi prompts in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`, three files must be updated in the same commit:
56	
57	1. `Dockerfile` — add `ARG CHEZMOI_*` build argument, add `--promptBool` / `--promptString` flag to `chezmoi init`.
58	2. `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` — add a matching entry to the `PROMPTS` tuple (key, kind, group, label, desc, default).
59	3. (If the prompt should be part of any named bundle) `BUNDLES` dict in the same file.
60	
61	Verify parity with: `uv run --script scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py doctor`. The subcommand greps `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` + `Dockerfile` and compares against the embedded `PROMPTS`; non-zero exit means drift.
62	
63	### Agent artifact redaction
64	
65	SpecStory transcripts and coding-agent plan files commonly paste shell output, config snippets, or `.env` values that may contain secrets. Four directories are auto-scanned/redacted:
66	
67	| Prefix | Source |
68	|--------|--------|
69	| `.specstory/history/` | SpecStory chat transcripts |
70	| `.claude/plans/` | Claude Code plan files |
71	| `.cursor/plans/` | Cursor plan files |
72	| `.opencode/plans/` | OpenCode plan files |
73	
74	Tooling: `scripts/redact_secrets.py` (gitleaks + `PRIV***KEY` pattern), `just check-secrets` / `just redact-secrets` / `just add-and-redact`. Pre-commit hook `redact-agent-secrets` runs `--fix` before `gitleaks-system`; if it rewrites a file, stage and retry.
75	
76	When introducing a new coding-agent artifact directory that could contain secrets, add its prefix to `DEFAULT_PATHS` in `scripts/redact_secrets.py` **and** the `files:` regex of the `redact-agent-secrets` pre-commit hook.
77	
78	### Keyboard shortcuts (cross-tool conflict check)
79	
80	When adding/modifying keybindings in any tool config, cross-check against other tools — multiple tools share the terminal's key namespace, especially `Ctrl+` and `Alt+`.
81	
82	| Tool | Config file | Conflict risk |
83	|------|-------------|---------------|
84	| tmux (root-table) | `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf` | `C-h/j/k/l` (vim-tmux-navigator), `C-1..9` (window switch); `prefix + a` (live agent panes picker — `tv agent-panes`, see [docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md](docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md)) |
85	| Television (global) | `dot_config/television/config.toml` | `Ctrl+S/F/R/Y/T/X/O` (built-in actions) |
86	| Television (channels) | `dot_config/television/cable/*.toml` | Per-channel `[keybindings]` overrides global |
87	| Zellij | `dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` | Mitigated by `default_mode "locked"` |
88	| Ghostty | `dot_config/ghostty/config` | `macos-option-as-alt` affects `Alt+` availability |
89	| zsh ZLE widgets | `dot_config/zsh/tools/{11_tools_picker,12_television,22_sesh,05_aisuggest}.zsh` | `Alt+T/R/P/G/E/A/I/S` (pickers), `Alt+;` (aisuggest, configurable via `AISUGGEST_KEY`); rebound from `zvm_after_init` in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` to survive zsh-vi-mode's keybind wipe |
90	| Claude Code (TUI) | `dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json` (overlay) + `~/.claude/keybindings.json` (live); see [docs/tools/claude-code-keybindings.md](docs/tools/claude-code-keybindings.md) | `Ctrl+R` (history:search — collides with atuin / zsh-history-substring at the prompt outside Claude), `Ctrl+T` (toggleTodos — Television's `Ctrl+T` is shadowed when Claude has focus), `Ctrl+G` (chat:externalEditor), `Ctrl+S` (chat:stash), `Shift+Tab` (chat:cycleMode — only known mode-switch action, no jump-to-plan) |
91	
92	Known conflict zones: `Ctrl+H/J/K/L` (tmux vim-tmux-navigator; removed in TV global), `Ctrl+S/F/R` (TV built-in cycling/reload — avoid in channel actions), `Alt+*` (safe namespace for channel-specific actions; requires terminal to send Option as Meta). Free Alt slots in this repo: `Alt+/`, `Alt+\`, and most letters not listed above (B/D/F/H/J/K/L/M/N/O/Q/U/V/W/X/Y/Z) — but check `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` first before claiming a new one.
93	
94	**Resolution precedence**: tmux root-table bindings intercept keys before they reach the inner application. Inside tmux, any `bind-key -n C-*` shadows the same `ctrl-*` in TV. Prefer `Alt+` for custom actions.

133	
134	## Chezmoi templating conventions
135	
136	**Hard rule**: before adding a `{{ if eq .profile ... }}` branch, ask if the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` / `.chezmoi.arch` / `.chezmoi.hostname` instead. `.profile` exists only for user-role choices chezmoi cannot infer (server vs desktop).
137	
138	| Predicate | Use |
139	|---|---|
140	| Any macOS (Apple Silicon or Intel) | `eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"` |
141	| Any Linux | `eq .chezmoi.os "linux"` |
142	| Apple Silicon only | `eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64"` (inside darwin-scoped files) or `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64")` |
143	| Intel Mac only | `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "amd64")` |
144	| Desktop vs headless (user role) | `.profile` — `ubuntu_desktop` / `ubuntu_server`; macOS side covered by `eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"` |
145	
146	Profile values are intentionally limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server`. **Do not** introduce new profile values for OS/arch facts (the historical `macos_intel` profile was removed for exactly this reason).
147	
148	Full decision table, before/after examples, and the `macos_intel` migration snippet: [docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).

- **`04_ai_capture.zsh`** → bash: keep `aifix`, `aiexplain`, `aiblock` verbatim; rewrite `print -u2` to `>&2`, handle `${=var}` array expansion (zsh only); likely 95% reusable

### C. IRREDUCIBLE ZSH-ONLY FEATURES (DROP ON BASH SIDE)

| Feature | File | Impact on User | Bash Fallback |
|---------|------|---|---|
| **aisuggest ZLE widget** (Alt+; ghost text UI) | `05_aisuggest.zsh` | Prompt-time NL→command suggestions **with interactive acceptor (Tab/→)**; full ZLE control over BUFFER, POSTDISPLAY, region_highlight | Bash: CLI form only — `aisuggest "text"` outputs command to stdout; no in-prompt ghost text or accept/reject UX |
| **Inline command history via tv widgets** (Alt+R/P/G/E/A/I) | `12_television.zsh` | Six interactive pickers bound to Alt keys; rely on ZLE line manipulation and `zle reset-prompt` | Bash: CLI-only fallback `tv <channel>` in a subshell; no direct line insertion; user must copy/paste manually or create fzf wrapper |
| **Tools picker widget** (Alt+T) | `11_tools_picker.zsh` | Interactive fzf-based CLI picker with Enter→paste, Ctrl+E→execute | Bash: Standalone fzf picker spawned in subshell; user manually pastes output or executes directly |
| **zsh-vi-mode plugin** (vi keybindings + hooks) | `dot_zshrc.tmpl` / plugins | Full vi mode in ZLE with custom keybindings; `zvm_after_init` hook chains zsh-specific plugins | Bash: Readline vi mode (`set -o vi`) is available but minimal; no hook system for re-binding after init; no native `zsh-autosuggestions` or `zsh-syntax-highlighting` equivalent on bash (oh-my-bash has compat versions, but less featured) |
| **zsh-autosuggestions widget** | oh-my-zsh plugin | Background history suggestion with ZLE prefix matching | Bash: oh-my-bash port exists but simpler UX |
| **OSC 133 shell integration hooks** | `02_shell_integration.zsh` | Prompt/preexec markers for tmux output nav via `add-zsh-hook` and PROMPT manipulation | Bash: Requires manual `PS1` crafting with escape sequences; no native hook system (would need `PROMPT_COMMAND`) |
| **Sesh-sessions ZLE widget** (Alt+S) | `22_sesh.zsh` | Interactive fzf picker that auto-connects to tmux session | Bash: Wrap `sesh list \| fzf` in a function; no direct LBUFFER paste, so user types `sesh connect <name>` manually or uses a different keybinding workflow |

### oh-my-zsh → oh-my-bash Plugin Mapping

From `dot_zshrc.tmpl` (lines 21–26):
```zsh
plugins=(
    git
    zsh-autosuggestions
    zsh-syntax-highlighting
    zsh-vi-mode
)
```

| ZSH Plugin | Equivalent in oh-my-bash | Status | Notes |
|------------|---------------------------|--------|-------|
| `git` | `git` plugin (aliases like `gst`, `ga`, etc.) | ✅ Exists | Same aliases available |
| `zsh-autosuggestions` | `autosuggestions` plugin | ⚠️ Simpler | oh-my-bash port exists; syntax highlighting in suggestions less sophisticated |
| `zsh-syntax-highlighting` | `syntax-highlighting` plugin | ✅ Exists | Bash version available in oh-my-bash |
| `zsh-vi-mode` | not native | ❌ N/A | Bash's `set -o vi` is built-in but no framework for custom hooks; manual keybinding via `.inputrc` for plugin-like setup |

**Recommendation:** 
- Use oh-my-bash with `git`, `autosuggestions`, `syntax-highlighting` plugins
- Set `set -o vi` in `.bashrc` for vi mode
- Accept that vi keybinding customization will be via `.inputrc` (less dynamic than zsh's hook system)
- Note that `zvm_after_init` hook (re-source fzf after vi-mode init) is zsh-specific; on bash, just source fzf early in `.bashrc` and let readline manage key states

From `05_aisuggest.zsh`, the pipeline is:

1. **`_aisuggest_query(input_text)`** — calls `_aiagent_invoke` with a system prompt (lines 146–211)
   - Pure shell function; calls agent CLI (claude/opencode/codex/cursor-agent)
   - Returns raw text from agent
   - **✅ 100% shell-agnostic**

2. **`_aisuggest_sanitize(text)`** — strips ANSI and control chars (lines 123–136)
   - Uses `while [[ ... ]]` and zsh parameter expansion `${...//...}`
   - **Can be rewritten to POSIX sed/tr:**
     ```bash

     }
     ```

3. **`_aisuggest_widget()`** — ZLE integration (lines 324–381)
   - **Irreducible ZLE:** `POSTDISPLAY`, `zle -R`, `read -k` (ZLE-aware read), `bindkey`, `zle -N`

**Bash equivalent:**
- Keep the agent backend and sanitizer
- CLI form: `aisuggest "<text>"` → prints command to stdout (already implemented in lines 454–560)
- No in-prompt ghost text or interactive accept/reject; user runs `aisuggest "find files"` separately and copies output

181	# Scaffold or update project-local .claude/settings.json so Claude Code's

193	# Usage: claude-plans-here [-f] [-y]

196	claude-plans-here() {
197	  emulate -L zsh
198	  local force_settings=0 force_orphans=0

202	      -y) force_orphans=1 ;;

223	  "plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"
224	}
225	EOF
226	    echo "Wrote $PWD/$target"
227	  else
228	    if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
229	      echo "claude-plans-here: jq required to merge into existing $target" >&2
230	      return 1
231	    fi

233	    local ans=y
234	    if (( ! force_settings )); then
235	      read -q "ans?$target exists. Merge plansDirectory into it? [y/N] " || { echo; ans=n; }

253	  _claude_plans_here_import_orphans "$force_orphans"

256	# Internal: scan ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd|encoded-git-root>/*.jsonl
257	# for Write/Edit tool_use entries that wrote into ~/.claude/plans/, list the
258	# ones still living in the global dir and not yet copied locally, prompt y/N.
259	_claude_plans_here_import_orphans() {
260	  emulate -L zsh
261	  setopt local_options null_glob
262	  local force="$1"
263	  local global_plans="$HOME/.claude/plans"

266	  # Claude Code projects/ encoding: replace each '/' and '.' with '-'.
267	  local enc_cwd="${PWD//\//-}"
268	  enc_cwd="${enc_cwd//./-}"

272	      enc_root="${groot//\//-}"

279	  [[ -n "$enc_root" && -d "$HOME/.claude/projects/$enc_root" ]] && proj_dirs+=("$HOME/.claude/projects/$enc_root")
280	  (( ${#proj_dirs} == 0 )) && return 0
281	
282	  local -a jsonl_files
283	  local d
284	  for d in "${proj_dirs[@]}"; do

286	  done
287	  (( ${#jsonl_files} == 0 )) && return 0

289	  # Two-stage filter: only lines containing a Write/Edit tool_use, then

291	  # paths that merely appeared in user/assistant text.
292	  local re_prefix="${global_plans//./\\.}"
293	  local -a matches

296	    [[ -n "$line" ]] && matches+=("$line")

299	      | grep -oE "${re_prefix}/[A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+\.md" \

301	  )

1	# OSC 133 shell integration — emits prompt/command markers so tmux can
2	# navigate command boundaries (next-prompt / previous-prompt in copy-mode)
3	# and the prefix + M-y binding in dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf can
4	# copy the last command's output (Warp-style).
5	#
6	# Protocol: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/Per_Bothner/specifications/blob/master/proposals/semantic-prompts.md
7	#
8	#   OSC 133 ; A ST             before prompt (start of prompt)
9	#   OSC 133 ; B ST             between prompt and command input (end of prompt)
10	#   OSC 133 ; C ST             after Enter, before command output (start of output)
11	#   OSC 133 ; D ; exit_code ST after command finishes (end of output)
12	#
13	# Uses add-zsh-hook so it chains cleanly after starship / zsh-vi-mode / oh-my-zsh
14	# (they all also use add-zsh-hook — no clobbering).
15	#
16	# Opt-out: export DISABLE_OSC133=1 before starting zsh.
17	
18	[[ -n "$DISABLE_OSC133" ]] && return
19	[[ "$TERM" == "dumb" ]] && return
20	
21	autoload -Uz add-zsh-hook
22	
23	_osc133_precmd() {
24	  local ec=$?
25	  # Wrap the (already-rendered-by-starship) PROMPT with D + A markers using
26	  # %{...%} so zsh treats them as zero-width. This runs AFTER starship's
27	  # own precmd (add-zsh-hook chains in registration order; 01_starship.zsh
28	  # loads before 02_shell_integration.zsh).
29	  #
30	  # Why in PROMPT, not printf? An earlier version printf'd A from precmd
31	  # directly. tmux's OSC 133 line-attr tracking was unreliable — ZLE's
32	  # cursor management between precmd and prompt-paint caused the A flag
33	  # to land on the wrong grid line (next-prompt navigation found zero A
34	  # markers even though the bytes were sent). Embedding via PROMPT
35	  # guarantees the markers render at the exact spatial location tmux
36	  # expects (start of the prompt line).
37	  #
38	  # D marker carries the previous command's exit code; A marks start of
39	  # new prompt. Neither is strictly required for next-prompt/previous-prompt
40	  # navigation (A is, D isn't), but both are cheap.
41	  PROMPT=$'%{\e]133;D;'"${ec}"$';\a\e]133;A\a%}'"${PROMPT}"
42	}
43	
44	_osc133_preexec() {
45	  # Skip C for our own tmux capture helpers — otherwise their copy-mode
46	  # `previous-prompt -o` chain lands on their own (empty) output start
47	  # instead of the previous command's real output. Coupling is documented
48	  # in 03_tmux_capture.zsh.
49	  case "${1%% *}" in
50	    cpout|cpcmd|cpblock) return ;;
51	  esac
52	  # C: start of command output (Enter was just pressed, before exec).
53	  printf '\e]133;C\a'
54	}
55	
56	add-zsh-hook precmd _osc133_precmd
57	add-zsh-hook preexec _osc133_preexec
58	
59	# B (end-of-prompt marker) would naturally append to PROMPT tail. tmux's
60	# next-prompt / previous-prompt only needs A and C, so we skip B. Revisit if
61	# a future consumer (Ghostty semantic shell integration, Warp) requires it.

1	# tmux + OSC 133 capture helpers — shell-level counterparts of the
2	# prefix + M-y / M-i tmux bindings, with an N-back index.
3	#
4	#   cpcmd [N]    last (or Nth-latest) command's INPUT  (zsh history; universal)
5	#   cpout [N]    last (or Nth-latest) command's OUTPUT (tmux copy-mode chain)
6	#   cpblock [N]  last (or Nth-latest) command's FULL BLOCK, Warp-style
7	#
8	# N defaults to 1 (= latest). N=2 is the one before that, and so on.
9	#
10	# Each prints captured text to stdout (pipe-friendly: `cpout | grep ERROR`)
11	# AND copies to system clipboard. Diagnostic + byte count go to stderr so
12	# stdout stays clean for pipes.
13	#
14	# WHY cpout/cpblock need tmux:
15	# tmux consumes OSC 133 marker bytes and only stores them as per-line
16	# attributes in its grid — `tmux capture-pane -pe` does NOT re-emit them.
17	# Outside tmux there's no portable way to recover boundaries of a past
18	# command's output (terminals like iTerm2/Ghostty have proprietary APIs,
19	# but nothing cross-terminal). cpcmd uses zsh shell history instead, so it
20	# works universally.
21	#
22	# Requires: zsh; plus tmux for cpout/cpblock.
23	
24	# Pipe stdin to system clipboard, preferring tmux's OSC 52 bridge (SSH-safe)
25	# and falling back to platform-native clipboard tools.
26	_cpx_to_clipboard() {
27	  if [[ -n "$TMUX" ]]; then
28	    tmux load-buffer -w -
29	  elif command -v pbcopy &>/dev/null; then
30	    pbcopy
31	  elif command -v wl-copy &>/dev/null; then
32	    wl-copy
33	  elif command -v xclip &>/dev/null; then
34	    xclip -selection clipboard -in
35	  elif command -v xsel &>/dev/null; then
36	    xsel --clipboard --input
37	  else
38	    cat >/dev/null
39	    return 1
40	  fi
41	}
42	
43	# Validate a positive-integer argument. Echoes the value on success; prints
44	# a usage hint to stderr and returns 1 on invalid input.
45	_cpx_parse_n() {
46	  local name=$1 n=${2:-1}
47	  if [[ ! "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( n < 1 )); then
48	    print -u2 "$name: N must be a positive integer (got: $n). Usage: $name [N]"
49	    return 1
50	  fi
51	  print -r -- "$n"
52	}
53	
54	# Run a tmux copy-mode selection chain on the current pane. Prints selection
55	# to stdout, diagnostic (name + byte count) to stderr. Returns 1 on empty.
56	#
57	#   _cpx_tmux_select <display-name> <prev-count> <prev-cmd> [prev-args...]
58	#
59	# Chain: copy-mode → (<prev-cmd> <prev-args...>) × <prev-count> →
60	#        begin-selection → next-prompt →
61	#        copy-pipe-and-cancel "tee <tmp> | tmux load-buffer -w -" → wait-for
62	#
63	# <prev-count> is how many times to repeat the `previous-*` command before
64	# starting the selection — that's how N-back lookback is done.
65	#
66	# Depends on 02_shell_integration.zsh skipping the OSC 133 C marker for
67	# these helpers' own invocation (see the case statement there). Without
68	# that skip, `previous-prompt -o` would land on this command's own output
69	# start and the selection would be empty.
70	_cpx_tmux_select() {
71	  local name=$1; shift
72	  local prev_count=$1; shift
73	  local tmp sentinel i _y
74	  tmp="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/cpx-$$-$RANDOM"
75	  sentinel="cpx-$$-$RANDOM"
76	  : > "$tmp"
77	  tmux copy-mode -t "$TMUX_PANE" 2>/dev/null || return 1
78	  # Seek to history bottom so N-back math is measured from a known origin.
79	  tmux send-keys -t "$TMUX_PANE" -X history-bottom 2>/dev/null
80	  # Sync barrier between `send-keys -X` calls: an assignment from
81	  # `$(tmux display-message -p …)` is what actually forces the tmux server
82	  # to commit the previous copy-mode command before it answers. Without
83	  # this round-trip, bursts of `previous-prompt` calls collapse to a single
84	  # cursor jump on tmux 3.6a — `sleep`, `: "$(…)"`, and bare redirection
85	  # (`>/dev/null`) are ALL insufficient. The variable read is what makes zsh
86	  # wait for subprocess output, which in turn serialises tmux's queue.
87	  for (( i = 0; i < prev_count; i++ )); do
88	    tmux send-keys -t "$TMUX_PANE" -X "$@" 2>/dev/null
89	    _y=$(tmux display-message -p -t "$TMUX_PANE" '#{copy_cursor_y}' 2>/dev/null)
90	  done
91	  tmux send-keys -t "$TMUX_PANE" -X begin-selection 2>/dev/null
92	  tmux send-keys -t "$TMUX_PANE" -X next-prompt 2>/dev/null
93	  _y=$(tmux display-message -p -t "$TMUX_PANE" '#{copy_cursor_y}' 2>/dev/null)
94	  tmux send-keys -t "$TMUX_PANE" -X copy-pipe-and-cancel \
95	    "tee $tmp | tmux load-buffer -w - ; tmux wait-for -S $sentinel" 2>/dev/null
96	  tmux wait-for "$sentinel" 2>/dev/null
97	  if [[ -s "$tmp" ]]; then
98	    cat "$tmp"
99	    local bytes
100	    bytes=$(wc -c <"$tmp" | tr -d ' ')
101	    rm -f "$tmp"
102	    print -u2 "$name: $bytes bytes copied to clipboard"
103	    return 0
104	  fi
105	  rm -f "$tmp"
106	  return 1
107	}
108	
109	# cpcmd [N] — last (or Nth-latest) command's INPUT. Universal: reads zsh
110	# shell history. Clean output (no prompt chrome, no terminal-echo artefacts).
111	cpcmd() {
112	  emulate -L zsh
113	  local n
114	  n=$(_cpx_parse_n cpcmd "${1:-1}") || return 1
115	  local cmd
116	  # fc -ln -N -N: list entries from (-N) to (-N), inclusive — just the Nth back
117	  cmd=$(fc -ln -"$n" -"$n" 2>/dev/null)
118	  cmd="${cmd#	}"   # strip fc's leading tab
119	  cmd="${cmd# }"
120	  if [[ -z "$cmd" ]]; then
121	    print -u2 "cpcmd: no command at N=$n in shell history"
122	    return 1
123	  fi
124	  printf '%s\n' "$cmd" | _cpx_to_clipboard || {
125	    print -u2 "cpcmd: no clipboard tool available (install pbcopy / xclip / xsel / wl-copy, or run inside tmux)"
126	    return 1
127	  }
128	  printf '%s\n' "$cmd"
129	  print -u2 "cpcmd: ${#cmd} bytes (zsh history -$n) copied to clipboard"
130	}
131	
132	# cpout [N] — last (or Nth-latest) command's OUTPUT via tmux's OSC 133 line
133	# attrs. cpout/cpcmd/cpblock themselves are preexec-skipped for C, so N=1
134	# lands on the *previous* command's output start, N=2 on the one before, etc.
135	cpout() {
136	  emulate -L zsh
137	  if [[ -z "$TMUX" ]]; then
138	    print -u2 "cpout: requires tmux (OSC 133 boundaries are stored per-pane by tmux). Use cpcmd for input, or your terminal's native 'copy output' if available."
139	    return 1
140	  fi
141	  local n
142	  n=$(_cpx_parse_n cpout "${1:-1}") || return 1
143	  _cpx_tmux_select "cpout -$n" "$n" previous-prompt -o || {
144	    print -u2 "cpout: empty at N=$n — (a) shell pre-dates chezmoi apply, run 'exec zsh' (verify: echo \$precmd_functions | grep osc133); (b) N exceeds command history in this pane; (c) target command is an alt-screen TUI (vim, htop) with no OSC 133 output."
145	    return 1
146	  }
147	}
148	
149	# cpblock [N] — last (or Nth-latest) command's FULL BLOCK (prompt + input +
150	# output), Warp-style. The OSC 133 A marker is embedded in PROMPT itself
151	# (02_shell_integration.zsh) so cpblock's OWN prompt carries an A too —
152	# call previous-prompt N+1 times to skip self + land N-back.
153	cpblock() {
154	  emulate -L zsh
155	  if [[ -z "$TMUX" ]]; then
156	    print -u2 "cpblock: requires tmux (see cpout for why)."
157	    return 1
158	  fi
159	  local n
160	  n=$(_cpx_parse_n cpblock "${1:-1}") || return 1
161	  _cpx_tmux_select "cpblock -$n" $(( n + 1 )) previous-prompt || {
162	    print -u2 "cpblock: empty at N=$n — run 'exec zsh' if the shell pre-dates chezmoi apply, or N exceeds command history in this pane."
163	    return 1
164	  }
165	}

190	
191	  if (( raw )); then
192	    _aiagent_invoke "$agent" "$prompt"
193	  else
194	    _aiagent_invoke "$agent" "$prompt" | _aicap_prettify
195	  fi
196	  local rc=$?
197	
198	  AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=$saved_show
199	  AICAP_PRETTIFY=$saved_pretty
200	  return $rc
201	}

203	# Print the shared flag-help + env-var snapshot. Used by -h on each wrapper.
204	_ai_print_help() {
205	  local name=$1 usage=$2
206	  print -r -- "usage: $name $usage"
207	  print -r -- "  -a AGENT   claude | opencode | codex | cursor-agent (default: auto-detect)"
208	  print -r -- "  -p PROMPT  override default prompt"
209	  print -r -- "  --raw      disable prettify (glow/bat), print raw agent reply"
210	  print -r -- "  --no-meta  suppress the stderr metadata line"
211	  print -r -- ""
212	  print -r -- "env vars:"
213	  print -r -- "  AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL   = ${AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL}"
214	  print -r -- "  AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL = ${AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL}"
215	  print -r -- "  AICAP_CODEX_MODEL    = ${AICAP_CODEX_MODEL}"
216	  print -r -- "  AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL   = ${AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL:-<unset>}"
217	  print -r -- "  AICAP_SHOW_METADATA  = ${AICAP_SHOW_METADATA}"
218	  print -r -- "  AICAP_PRETTIFY       = ${AICAP_PRETTIFY}"
219	  print -r -- "  AICAP_SPINNER        = ${AICAP_SPINNER}"
220	}
221	
222	# Shared dispatcher for aifix / aiexplain. Captures via cpblock.
223	_ai_capture_dispatch() {
224	  emulate -L zsh
225	  local name=$1; shift
226	  local default_prompt=$1; shift
227	  local n=1 agent="" prompt_override="" raw=0 no_meta=0
228	  while (( $# )); do
229	    case "$1" in
230	      -a|--agent)   agent=$2; shift 2 ;;
231	      -p|--prompt)  prompt_override=$2; shift 2 ;;
232	      --raw)        raw=1; shift ;;
233	      --no-meta)    no_meta=1; shift ;;
234	      -h|--help)    _ai_print_help "$name" "[N] [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT] [--raw] [--no-meta]"
235	                    print -r -- "  N          block index back (default 1 = last)"
236	                    return 0 ;;
237	      --) shift; break ;;
238	      -*) print -u2 "$name: unknown flag: $1"; return 1 ;;
239	      *)  n=$1; shift ;;
240	    esac
241	  done
242	  if [[ ! "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( n < 1 )); then
243	    print -u2 "$name: N must be a positive integer (got: $n)"
244	    return 1
245	  fi
246	  if [[ -z "$agent" ]]; then
247	    agent=$(_aiagent_autodetect) || {
248	      print -u2 "$name: no coding-agent CLI found on PATH (tried: claude, opencode, codex, cursor-agent)"
249	      return 1
250	    }
251	  fi
252	  local block
253	  block=$(cpblock "$n" 2>/dev/null) || {
254	    print -u2 "$name: cpblock $n failed (run 'exec zsh' if the shell pre-dates chezmoi apply)"
255	    return 1
256	  }
257	  _ai_dispatch_core "$name" "block -$n" "$default_prompt" \
258	    "$agent" "$raw" "$no_meta" "$prompt_override" "$block"
259	}
260	
261	aifix() {
262	  _ai_capture_dispatch aifix \
263	    "Here is a command I ran in my terminal and its output. Diagnose any errors and suggest a concrete fix. Be brief and specific." \
264	    "$@"
265	}
266	
267	aiexplain() {
268	  _ai_capture_dispatch aiexplain \
269	    "Here is a command I ran in my terminal and its output. Explain what happened in plain language. Be concise." \
270	    "$@"
271	}
